full_judgment:
Md Abdur Rashid J: Defendant No. 1 presented the appeal against an order dated 21-4-2003 passed by the District Judge at Chittagong in Miscellaneous Case No. 27 of 2003, which dismissed the case as not maintainable. 

 4. Thereafter, on 5-2-03 the appellant made an application under Order XLI, rule 19 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure being Miscellaneous Case No. 27 of 2003 for re- admission of the appeal. 

 5. In the application, it is stated that on 17-10-02 when the case was fixed for filing of deficit court fees he was sick. On 15-10-02 he was attacked with Hepatitis and confined to bed. For want of any instructions, learned Advocate could not take any step. Recovered, he on 20-1-03 saw his Advocate's clerk and came to know definitely about the rejection of the memo of appeal. 

 6. On hearing the application, learned District Judge found the case barred by limitation and also not maintainable since the order rejecting the memorandum of appeal was appealable. Upon such view, he dismissed the case by impugned order. 

 9. Mr Momtazuddin Ahmed, learned Senior Advocate on behalf of the respondent, however, defended the order of the learned District Judge and submitted that miscellaneous case brought under Order XLI, rule, 19 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure was wholly misconceived and the learned District Judge rightly found the same not maintainable. 

 "Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) or in any other Act, a Court may receive a plaint or memorandum of appeal in respect of which an insufficient fee has been paid, subject to the condition that the plaint of “memorandum of appeal shall be rejected unless the plaintiff or appellant, as the case may be,pays to the Court within a time to be fixed by the Court such reasonable sum on account of court fees as the Court may direct." 

 20. In Abdul Aziz vs Tofazzal Hossain, 50 DLR 487 another single Bench of this Division made a Rule issued upon a revision application made under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure absolute and set aside an order of a District Judge which allowed the appellant time to file deficit court fees beyond the statutory period of 21 days as per the proviso to Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and rejected the memo of appeal. In none of the cases, whether or not such order rejecting a memorandum of appeal for non-supply of deficit court fees or accepting court fees beyond time was revisable under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure was not 'raised. Nor any view was expressed thereto. 

 23. Limitation now imposed upon the discretion of a Court in granting time for supply of requisite stamp-paper by proviso to rule 11 of Order VII of the Code of Civil Procedure not exceeding 21 days shall, in our view, equally apply in case of a memorandum of appeal. The discretion of the Court under section 149 in extending time must therefore be read subject to proviso to rule 11 of Order VII of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 24. In the case, granting so much time by so many orders beyond the period of limitation for payment of deficit court fees first up to 17-10-2002 and then, by issuing notice to show cause against possible rejection of the imam of appeal up to 11-11-02 is therefore, not sanctioned by law. 

 25. We also find no reason to disagree with the view taken in Radha Rani vs Durga Rani Adhikari, 47 DLR 360 that in an appropriate case, a Court may invoke inherent jurisdiction under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to accept the deficit court fees and admit the appeal after setting aside its order rejecting the memorandum of appeal. It is needless to say such power could only be exercised within the periphery of the above provisions of law. 

 26. In the case at hand, on 20-6-02 the memorandum of appeal was presented and the District Judge rejected said memorandum of appeal after giving time on several occasions, beyond the period of limitation. Then, on 5-2-03 the appellant made the application under Order XLI, rule 19 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure without deposit of the deficit court fees. Even if we consider as was fervently urged on behalf of the appellant the application as one under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure that would not rescue him. First, the application was hopelessly barred by limitation and secondly, it was made without deposit of deficit court fees. Lastly, the explanation for the delay in making the application does not inspire any confidence.
